pr_title: Add support for java.util.Optional to GenericHttpMessageConverter #24498
pr_body:
Fixes #24498

Added unboxing of  `java.util.Optional`  to `AbstractHttpMessageConverter` and `AbstractGenericHttpMessageConverter`. If the object is not unboxed, the underlying message converter receives an instance of `java.util.Optional`, which was causing an issue described in the #24498 in case of Jackson converter. It will also allow to use `Optional<*>` in other message converters without explicitly registering a type converter.
pr_comments: @sbrannen just a kind reminder. Lets review&merge or close it if you think that such behaviour should not be part of the product

Thank for for submitting a PR, and our apologies for taking this long to resolve it.

We have decided to resolve the underlying issue differently than suggested in this PR,  in the Jackson converters rather than the generic converters. See https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/commit/5502e6151967afaef7fa3d9d057f3e2d226a0c84 for more details.

issue_context.title: Support Optional in Jackson 2 message converters
issue_context.body:

Given an endpoint that returns a polymorphic JSON type, eg.

```java
@JsonTypeInfo(use = JsonTypeInfo.Id.NAME)
@JsonSubTypes({Impl1.class, Impl2.class})
public interface Parent {
}

public class Impl1 implements Parent {
}

public class Impl2 implements Parent {
}

@GetMapping(produces = MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON_VALUE)
public Parent get() {
    return new Impl1();
}
```

Jackson will serialize it with the property `@type`, eg.
```json
{
    "@type": "Impl1"
}
```

However, when wrapping it with an `Optional`/[Page](https://docs.spring.io/spring-data/commons/docs/current/api/org/springframework/data/domain/Page.html), the JSON polymorphism no longer works. Eg.
```java
@GetMapping(produces = MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON_VALUE)
public Optional<Parent> getOptional() {
    return Optional.of(new Impl1());
}
```
returns:
```json
{}
```

According to FasterXML/jackson-databind#1594 this is due to type erasure, however the JSON polymorphism still works when wrapping with built-in `Collection`s (eg. `List`/`Set`/`Map`), eg.
```java
@GetMapping(produces = MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON_VALUE)
public Collection<Parent> getCollection() {
    return Collections.singleton(new Impl1());
}
```

So it seems like Spring has special handling for built-in `Collection`s. Is it possible to apply them to `Optional`/[Page](https://docs.spring.io/spring-data/commons/docs/current/api/org/springframework/data/domain/Page.html) as well?

Currently the workaround is to create custom `JsonSerializer`s for `Optional`/[Page](https://docs.spring.io/spring-data/commons/docs/current/api/org/springframework/data/domain/Page.html), eg.
```java
@JsonComponent
public class OptionalSerializer extends JsonSerializer<Optional<?>> {
    @Override
    public void serialize(Optional<?> value, JsonGenerator gen, SerializerProvider serializers) throws IOException {
        if (value.isPresent()) {
            gen.writeObject(value.get());
        }
    }
}
```
comments:
Hi.

I can confirm this issue. It works for collections thanks to Jackson support.

My PR fixes "Optional" only, for the Page it should be placed in a different repo I believe, spring-data-rest maybe?
I can confirm this too. Took me a while to find the cause of my problem.
I don't see a way for Spring Framework to support Spring Data's `Page` type, so `JsonSerializer`s will still be required for those, but I can add support for `Optional`.
This is now fixed. Our apologies for taking this long to resolve this issue.
@poutsma Thank you! Should I request support for `Page` in [spring-data-commons](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-data-commons) instead?

review_comments:
Quick question(s) about the unwrapping and returning type parameter: basically what ur doing here is convert a wrapped (Optional) value of type `T` to an unwrapped value and in the process of this changing the returned type. 
How are you going to be ensuring type safety? Especially for the abstract method `writeInternal` which may be implemented by anyone? Why would you always want to unwrap an Optional? Even when the original issue was with Jackson specifically?

Let's say that you have type argument `Optional<String>` and the `unboxIfNeeded` method converts this type to `String`. This all while `writeInternal` and the rest of the code still expect `T` to be `Optional<String>`, this especially is an issue since you tell the compiler to expect type safety (by suppressing the warning). 
These seem like mismatching types which might, depending on the implementing code, throw a ClassCastException. 

This may fix the issue, but you will now not know what the type of variable `t` really is going to be. When you implement `AbstractHttpMessageConverter` by yourself, you are going to be having restrictions for a fix on Jackson's implementation. I would suggest not changing this class but look at the Jackson specific implementation (`AbstractJackson2HttpMessageConverter`) since you won't be needing the type safety here and it tackles this specific issue.

_(I am fully aware that using Optional as a type argument is a bad practice, however I would value type safety over implementation of the user)_
Correct, in case when a converter has generic type `Optional<*>`, it would fail with the class cast exception. I will fix that

I see that you are now "ensuring" type safety. However, there are still some issues which resolve around the second part of my comment. And this part is crucial for the implementing side.

In my comment I mentioned the following:
> This may fix the issue, but you will now not know what the type of variable t really is going to be. When you implement AbstractHttpMessageConverter by yourself, you are going to be having restrictions for a fix on Jackson's implementation. I would suggest not changing this class but look at the Jackson specific implementation (AbstractJackson2HttpMessageConverter) since you won't be needing the type safety here and it tackles this specific issue.

With this, I was referring to the strategy pattern used by these classes (`HttpMessageConverter`, `GenericHttpMessageConverter`, `AbstractHttpMessageConverter` and `AbstractGenericHttpMessageConverter`). These classes are to be implemented and allow the user to define, at run-time, the to be chosen strategy. 
Since this is the case, we do not want the user to be confused or to already have some sort of pre-processing on any implementation that has been made. Because this specific issue (the unboxing issue) lies within the `AbstractJackson2HttpMessageConverter` class and sub classes: why not fix it there as it will fit that specific use case? Now we are going to be introducing bugs and unexpected behavior for anyone implementing this base class in it's own converter, which is most certainly not what we would want.
As agreed here #24867, we want to avoid code duplication. You are still able to override the `unboxIfNeeded` in the impl in case you really don't want the `Optional` to be unwrapped
